key_insight: LLM judges detect unsafe clinical actions more reliably with EHR evidence, while agent reasoning adds no overall benefit.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating clinical AI agents requires checking their actions against patient records, not relying on apparently successful final answers.
method: Injected controlled clinical errors into verified MedAgentBench trajectories.
Compared 416 faulty trajectories across eight error categories with correct counterparts using six open-weight LLM judges.
Varied access to final answers, action trajectories, EHR responses, and agent reasoning.
evidence_signal: Full-trajectory evaluation reached a discrimination score of 0.75; combining LLM judges with a full-EHR-informed rule-based checker detected 97% of injected faults.
watch_item: These benchmark results use injected faults and do not establish reliability in real-world clinical deployment.
paper_title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
